records.name: vsim — "Remotion for real 3D" (pure-TS software rasteriser)
findings: Architecture: zod-validated JSON scene document -> pure-TS rasteriser -> MP4; no GPU, no Chrome, no node-gyp.
Determinism is enforced, not promised: Math.random is lint-banned in runtime code and CI compares golden-frame hashes.

Feature set worth copying conceptually: per-pixel PBR with normal maps, PCF shadows, sorted transparency, ACES tone mapping, bloom, sky-derived hemisphere ambient, linear fog, glTF skeletal clips with crossfades, ground-contact IK with stance locking, spring bones, morph-target lip-sync, Rapier physics, beat-driven audio.
manga style is a single flag (style:"manga") that swaps to cel shading + ink outlines - a good precedent for exposing a "look" as one switch.
Speed verdict: 2040 ms/frame is ~14x too slow for our 9:16 1080x1920 workload next to a Skia path at 123-148 ms/frame.

Film3D pipeline is the most reusable idea: a director LLM writes a schema-validated Film3DDoc (cast, beats, shots), a compiler lowers it to a scene, and the renderer stays AI-free and deterministic. It also renders its own dailies and re-blocks from them.
evidence: cloned, pnpm 9.15.0 install + build succeeded
rendered examples 01-cube, 09-manga, 21-mouse at 1080x1920
benchmarked 2040 ms/frame @1080x1920 on 2 cores

records.name: Film3DDoc: validated screenplay -> scene compiler -> self-reviewed dailies
findings: Contract: the model may only emit a validated document; it never touches the render loop. A bad scene cannot be rendered, only rejected.
Shot vocabulary we should adopt: wide / close / follow / orbit, plus an optional handheld drift for documentary feel.
Self-review loop: one still per shot, two rounds, later rounds see the previous round frames. This is an automated visual QA gate that costs almost nothing.
Baking trick: HTML artifacts are baked to a frame sequence by a pinned headless Chromium and played back as an in-world texture. With our new browser cell this becomes available to us.
evidence: README film/3d section + package.json scripts read from raw.githubusercontent via page fetcher
read film:gen and film3d:fox scripts

anim.py is the whole architecture: spec JSON -> fill __SPEC__/__DURATION__ into template.html -> hyperframes render --fps 30 -q high -> contact sheet with Instagram safe area drawn in red.

records.name: @sparticuz/chromium — Chromium binary shipped inside the npm tarball
findings: This is the single enabler that turned "no browser is obtainable" into "a browser is obtainable" in a network-locked sandbox: the binary travels in the npm tarball, not a CDN.
The AL2023 archive is only auto-extracted when the package detects Amazon Linux 2023, so on Debian-like images the NSS libraries are present but never unpacked. Extract them manually.
SwiftShader tar (libEGL, libGLESv2, libvk_swiftshader, vulkan ICD) ships too, and its vulkan ICD json uses a RELATIVE library_path that must be rewritten to an absolute path before use.
evidence: npm install produced 75 MB node_modules, extracted a 227,736,800 B executable to /tmp/chromium
binary initially failed: "error while loading shared libraries: libnspr4.so"
apt has no libnspr4 and deb.debian.org is unreachable (HTTP 000)
found libnspr4.so / libnss3.so inside its own bin/al2023.tar.br; brotli-decompressed and tar-extracted; Chromium 158.0.8127.0 then started

records.name: Headless WebGL via ANGLE/SwiftShader in this sandbox
findings: Do not retry this: the failure is inside ANGLE/Vulkan initialisation, not in our flags or environment.
Keep the swiftshader libs extracted anyway - they cost nothing and would be the first thing to try if the image changes.
evidence: 7 flag combinations tried: --use-gl=angle|swiftshader, --use-angle=swiftshader|swiftshader-webgl|vulkan, --in-process-gpu, --headless=old, Vulkan feature flags
3 ICD configurations: package default, absolute library_path rewrite, VK_DRIVER_FILES
Chrome stderr: "Internal Vulkan error (-3)" at vk_renderer.cpp initialize:2546, then "eglInitialize SwANGLE failed with error EGL_NOT_INITIALIZED"
/dev/shm is 2.0 GB and all three SwiftShader libs resolve their deps, so neither memory nor missing libs explain it
records.reason: eglInitialize SwANGLE failed with EGL_NOT_INITIALIZED in every configuration tried; three.js is therefore unreachable in this sandbox

records.name: studio/src/render3d.mjs — software 3D on the Skia canvas
findings: Technique set: lookAt + perspective, backface cull, painter sort, Lambert key + hemisphere fill + rim, ACES tone mapping, contact shadows, 2x supersampling.
Framing rule for 9:16: horizontal half-extent is d*tan(fov/2)*(9/16), so width binds before height. A 4.6-unit set needs d~16.6 at fov 30; keep sets ~2.5 units and camera at 8.6 with fov 34.
Limitation: box-only. No meshes, no rigs, no textures, no cel shading.

records.name: zach-3d-films / five-styles contact sheets (11 skills)
findings: The gap to the reference look is not mesh fidelity: it is (1) a broad stretched specular on curved metal, (2) depth of field with a crisp subject and soft ground, (3) exaggerated proportion, (4) impact read as concentric rings plus one verb.
Reference staging grammar: one subject, one prop, one action verb, large negative space above.
Caption grammar: white bold lowercase bottom-centre ~6% of frame height with a soft drop shadow, no box.
Cheap wins identified for our channel: rounded label chips, impact rings, hairline-on-black variant, yellow no-box captions, DOF.

records.name: Visual QA gates: caption collision + motion-energy floor
findings: The existing 100/100 automated score did not catch either defect, so the score is measuring the wrong things.
Both are mechanically detectable: text/chart bounding-box intersection, and per-second frame-difference energy below a floor.
Because frames are the only way I can evaluate motion, these gates are the substitute for watching the video - they should be mandatory before any render is called done.

records.name: zach-d-films engine: PMREM softbox, Bokeh, Bloom, grade, lathe humans
findings: PMREM env built from explicit emissive planes (key 8x4 @3.2, rim 4x10 @1.6, fill 10x3 @1.0) prefilters reflections -> the broad directional specular; this is the highest-value technique
Post chain order: RenderPass -> BokehPass -> UnrealBloom(0.25*0.6, thr 1.6) -> OutputPass -> grade(vignette 0.28 aspect-compensated, grain 0.018)
Renders at 720x1280 not 1080x1920; deliberate cost trade

Characters have no rig and no mesh: LatheGeometry over a smoothstep-interpolated radius profile torsoR(y), 11 keys, scaled elliptically 1.13 x 1 x 0.66; armour shells are offset lathes with a Gaussian sternum ridge
All textures are procedural canvas2d from a seeded RNG: steel = blotches+scratches+pits as roughness with screen-blended colour map; chainmail = alternating tilted ellipse rings + bump map
Render contract: window.renderAt(t) -> page.screenshot(clip) -> PNG pipe -> ffmpeg libx264 crf 17; shots cached lazily by index
Per-frame lighting is returned by the shot (dof/bloom/exposure) instead of being a global setting - transferable immediately
Caption: triple-layer text-shadow + 0.6px dark stroke, 46px on 1280 (~3.6% of height), heavy grotesque, negative tracking
evidence: api.github.com git/trees listed 111 entries; identified the engine files the upload omitted

records.name: bean-cartoon 2D vector character engine (studio/src/cartoon.mjs)
findings: Style recovery: the viral reference frame (image-3.png) is 2D VECTOR, not shaded 3D. Verified by reading its construction: self-coloured outlines (darkened fill, never black ink) and flat fills with at most one hard shadow tone.
Key correction to round 2: skin is a FLAT fill with no shadow tone. A dark crescent across the cheek reads as a stain. Shading tones belong to clothing only.

Face is a data table: 9 expressions x (2 eye kinds, 2 brow offsets, 1 mouth kind). Eye kinds lid|happy|squeeze|shock|dot, mouths dash|grin|frown|o|smirk|teeth|laugh. All features derive from E = eye radius = 0.155 rx, which is why the face reads identically at 200px and 1280px.
Head is ~42% of total height with no neck: the single strongest style cue. Mitt hands, 2-bone IK limbs, stubby tube legs.

API traps fixed and recorded: (1) walkCycle must return OFFSETS not absolutes, or hands land below the feet; (2) raised arms must be drawn AFTER the head or the hands vanish behind the skull; (3) two same-coloured legs merge into one dark column in front view - the far leg needs a darker tone; (4) squish must floor at 0.70 or a front-view skull squashed sideways reads as a thin egg rather than a profile.
Round 7: artifact paths repointed to tracked mirrors in research/artifacts/characters (studio/out originals are gitignored, absent in fresh checkout)
evidence: charsheet.mjs renders 4 PNG contact sheets and a 150-frame 1080x1920 clip at 171-178 ms/frame

9 defects found and fixed by viewing output: missing hair, torso shade spilling outside the body, crossed legs, oversized vacant skull, hidden raised arms, hands below feet, merged legs, cheek stain, wart-like nose

records.name: jonhelpangan-jpg/cartoon-short-kit — '2D look, 3D motion' house style (rig3d.js, stick.js)
findings: LOOK.flat = THREE.MeshToonMaterial with a two-step gradientMap: flat colour plus exactly one hard shadow tone. LOOK.bean scales the head to [0.94, 1.12, 0.94]. This is the mechanism behind the entire look.
Faces are painted onto a canvas texture with plain 2D calls (drawFace3D -> faceFront), so the expression system is canvas2d code, not shader work - which is why it ports to us without WebGL.

FACE table: 14 expressions (neutral, stern, grin, laugh, whistle, nervous, shock, relief, relief_open, dazed, pained, smile, smile_closed, lick) over 5 eye kinds and 11 mouths. Feature positions are expressed in units of u = headWidth/100, so the face scales with the head.
Their rigs still need WebGL, so the reference cannot run here. Only the style and the face-table idea were carried over.

records.name: claude-animation-skills / low-poly
findings: The resolution ladder is the single biggest lever on CPU: render small, upscale nearest-neighbour. Also: ordered dither at 15-bit plus vertex snapping is what makes low-poly read as PS1 rather than as 'bad 3D'.
Both paths verified: 360x640->3x at 36.7 ms/frame, native 1080x1920 at 172.1 ms/frame.
evidence: template.html inspected (34917 B): 360x640 internal render upscaled 3x nearest-neighbour, PS1 vertex snap in project_vertex, 15-bit Bayer 4x4 dither in dithering_fragment, NearestFilter pixel textures 16-64px, PerspectiveCamera fov 52, Fog 10-30. Reimplemented in canvas2d as studio/src/lowpoly.mjs; measured 36.7 ms/frame vs 438 ms previous best.

records.name: Painter's-algorithm software rasteriser (own implementation)
findings: Terrain must be a separate pre-pass: painter's algorithm cannot interleave a ground plane with objects standing on it. Near-plane clipping is mandatory or the ground tears open in front of the camera.
Verified both render targets
evidence: 380 faces, 360x640: render 8.5 ms, post 4.1 ms, upscale 3.1 ms. 1080x1920: render 11.5 ms, post 40.3 ms. Post pass folded tint+grain+dither into one pixel loop: 33.4 ms -> 4.1 ms at 360x640.

records.name: @napi-rs/canvas context filter (gaussian blur)
findings: This Skia build exposes ctx.filter, giving cheap gaussian blur with no WebGL: the missing piece for volumetric light, soft shadows and bloom.
Used for cloud softening, snow dabs and volumetric masks
evidence: Probed: g.filter='blur(10px)' applies a real gaussian (centre 240, +2px 99, +8px 48, +40px 3). Used for cloud softening, snow texture dabs and soft occlusion masks.

records.name: Procedural sound design (own synthesis)
findings: A whole soundtrack can be generated with zero external assets: wind = cascaded one-pole low-pass on white noise; footsteps = enveloped filtered noise; a train horn = four detuned sines with vibrato; whoosh = swept one-pole low-pass.
Master verified at -1.5 dBFS peak with no clipped samples
evidence: 10 cues synthesised from noise shaping + additive sines; 16-bit 44.1k stereo master, peak -1.5 dBFS, RMS -16.17 dBFS, crest 14.67 dB, DC -1.4e-4, 0 clipped samples. Band energy low 0.131 / mid 0.075 / high 0.036.

records.name: Piper (rhasspy/piper) neural TTS
findings: Neural TTS is possible here with zero network access to model hubs, because some MIT repos vendor Piper voices directly in their tree. This is the single biggest quality jump in Round 5: formant synthesis (espeak) sounds 1985, Piper sounds human.
evidence: piper-tts 1.8.0 + onnxruntime 1.32 from PyPI. Model en_US-amy-medium (63 MB ONNX) fetched via api.github.com from Mobile-Artificial-Intelligence/babylon (MIT) because huggingface.co and cdn-lfs return HTTP 000. Measured: 0.40 s to synthesise 5.7 s of speech (14x realtime) on 2 cores; no GPU.

records.name: espeak-ng phoneme + word event timing
findings: Use espeak for TIMING and IPA only; use Piper for audio. Note GPL-3.0: fine for generating audio, but redistribution of the binary would carry the licence.
evidence: espeakng-loader 0.2.4 (PyPI) bundles libespeak-ng.so 1.52 + espeak-ng-data, 10 MB, no root. Synthesis callback exposes word events (type 1) with audio_position in ms, and espeak_TextToPhonemes with espeakCHARS_IPA returns one IPA cluster per word. Phoneme events (type 7) are compiled out of this build (espeak_SetParameter(21,1,0) returns -1).

records.name: IPA viseme set for lip-sync (own implementation)
findings: Phoneme-driven mouth shapes beat amplitude lip-flap: an 'm' closes the lips and an 'o' rounds them, which amplitude cannot express.
evidence: 53 IPA symbols mapped to mouth parameters {mouthOpen, mouthWide, mouthCurve}; diacritics stripped before lookup; co-articulation blends 30% toward the next phoneme 45 ms early. 57 phonemes driven in exp5-voice.mp4.

records.name: Procedural character mesh + 26-joint rig (own implementation)
findings: Rounded tubes and superellipsoids render flat-shaded at the same cost as boxes, so there is no reason to model a character out of boxes. Screen-space-independent: face features must be placed against a skullZ(x,y) surface function, not at fixed depths.
evidence: 2548 faces per figure at rest. Skeleton: 26 bones (root/hips/spine/chest/neck/head/jaw + shoulder/upperArm/foreArm/hand x2 + thigh/shin/foot/toe x2), FK with R=Ry*Rx*Rz per bone. Analytic two-bone IK with pole vector. Continuous expression space (7 params) with 10 named presets and blending; viseme set keyed on IPA.

records.name: Procedural locomotion + performance (own implementation)
findings: Feet must be IK targets, not joint angles: angle-driven legs skate. Arm poses must ALSO be IK targets — three composed pitch rotations put a 'guard' pose above the character's head.
evidence: Walk/run cycles via IK foot targets (planted during stance, arcs during swing), jump arc with anticipation/land/recover, impact with wind/strike/recoil/settle, idle breathing. Camera shake from squared trauma with layered band-limited noise; traumaDecay e^-kt.

records.name: Lens stack: DOF, bloom, grain, CA (own implementation)
findings: Chromatic aberration must be composited from three ISOLATED channels. Multiplying copies by pure red/blue and adding them doubles those channels against the untouched frame and turns the whole picture magenta.
evidence: 3-radius depth-slicing DOF via ctx.filter blur; bloom bright-pass at threshold 0.80 + blur + lighter; cached grain layer offset per frame; 3-channel chromatic aberration. fitFov() bisects the lens so subject points fit a safe rect in 22 iterations.

records.name: Fresnel rim light for flat-shaded night scenes (own implementation)
findings: A flat-shaded subject in a night scene with only key+hemispheric fill reads as unlit cardboard because nothing on its silhouette is brighter than the background. Rim + Fresnel is the cheapest fix. Also: a wall whose albedo matches the sky value makes lit windows look like paper rectangles glued to the sky - pale cornice/plinth/pilaster bands draw the building outline for 2 boxes.
evidence: rim={eye,dir,colour,intensity,power} added to shadeFace. k = (1-|n.v|)^power * max(0,-n.dir) * intensity. In the night scene at intensity 0.85 the rim was invisible; 1.75 with power 1.9 reads clearly. Plus groundPass hook so contact shadows are not buried by the terrain pre-pass.
